Reconcile every Stripe webhook endpoint's enabled_events with what subscription-webhook actually handles
Rationale: a handler Stripe never sends an event to is dead code that reads as working — no error, no log; three invoice handlers sat unused this way
Rationale: runs INSIDE Supabase so the four account/mode Stripe secrets never leave the function environment
Rationale: additive only — never removes an event someone added by hand for a reason this repo does not know
Dry run by default: POST {} previews the diff, only {"apply": true} writes to Stripe
Sweeps the uk/uae x test/live account matrix; a key not held for a combination is skipped, not an error
Auth accepts the raw service-role key OR an active super admin, so the reconciler can be driven from inside the database
An endpoint already subscribed to '*' is reported as covered and left untouched
SUBSCRIPTION_WEBHOOK_EVENTS is the shared source of truth binding the handler code to Stripe-side subscription config
Hourly pg_cron sweep running Tesla Supercharger sync for every tenant with the integration enabled
One tenant's sync failure is caught and reported per-tenant rather than aborting the whole sweep
Cron and the portal refresh button share one per-tenant sync engine (_shared/tesla-sync-engine.ts), so behaviour cannot diverge
User-initiated Supercharger charge sync behind the portal refresh button
A requested tenantId that is not the caller's own is rejected unless the caller is a super admin
Refuses to sync unless tenants.integration_tesla_fleet is true
Optional rentalId/vehicleId narrows a manual sync to one booking or car; the cron path always runs tenant-wide
Tesla Fleet API tenant integration console: OAuth connect, VIN compatibility check, list vehicles, status, disconnect
The same function serves Tesla's OAuth redirect over GET, so one generic redirect_uri works for every tenant
Rationale: the HMAC-signed OAuth state is the gate that stops an attacker forging a callback pointing at another tenant
One cross-tenant guard helper applied to every authenticated action instead of per-branch checks
Tesla tokens live in Supabase Vault; the storing RPC also flips tenants.integration_tesla_fleet to true as a side effect
A VIN found in the tenant's Tesla account flips vehicles.tesla_fleet_enabled and stores the Tesla vehicle id
Disconnect clears the Vault tokens and resets tesla_fleet_enabled/tesla_fleet_vehicle_id on every vehicle of the tenant
Trax's plain-English 'why this price' narrative for a pricing suggestion
Rationale: the math already decided the number — the model may only paraphrase a deterministic fact sheet, never invent figures
public.trax_price_suggest RPC — the structured breakdown this function is handed and only explains
The explanation is grounded in cross-tenant network comparables (p25/median/p75) plus the vehicle's own 90-day utilisation
Voice contract enforced in the system prompt: first name once, 2-3 sentences, plain prose, acknowledge a small comparable set
If the model returns nothing a templated sentence is built from the same comps, so the UI always has copy
A breakdown with confidence 'none' short-circuits to a fixed apology before any model call is made
Inbound SMS lands in the tenant's unified customer chat thread
Tenant is identified by matching the Twilio To number against tenants.twilio_phone_number, retried with/without the + prefix
Customer resolution: exact phone match, then a full-table scan comparing digits-only and suffix matches
Get-or-create one chat_channels row per (tenant, customer) so an inbound message never has nowhere to land
Messages from unrecognised numbers are kept in sms_unknown_threads instead of being dropped
The Twilio MessageSid is stored as external_id — the join key the delivery-status webhook later updates against
Every inbound message stamps chat_channels.last_message_at/last_channel so the omnichannel inbox can sort and badge
Always answers Twilio with an empty 200 TwiML, even on internal failure, so Twilio does not retry a poisoned message
Inbound WhatsApp lands in the same unified chat thread, tagged channel='whatsapp'
Tenant resolved against tenants.twilio_whatsapp_number — a column distinct from the SMS twilio_phone_number
Twilio's 'whatsapp:' address prefix is stripped from From and To before any matching
The same exact-then-suffix customer phone resolution as the SMS webhook, re-implemented rather than shared
Unknown WhatsApp senders are stored in the SMS-named sms_unknown_threads/sms_unknown_messages tables
Twilio delivery-status receiver that moves a sent message through queued/sent/delivered/failed
Status lands by external_id: chat_channel_messages first, then sms_unknown_messages if no row matched
The full Twilio form payload plus error code/message is archived in sms_message_log for deliverability forensics
Always returns 200 to Twilio, even on internal error, to stop callback retries
Outbound click-to-call: TwiML that dials the customer from the browser client using the tenant's caller ID
Tenant is identified by the Twilio AccountSid on the request — the BYO (bring-your-own) Twilio account is the tenant key
The browser client identity 'client:tenant_{app_user_id}' encodes which staff member placed the call, and becomes call_logs.caller_id
When call_recording_enabled, a spoken consent line is prepended and record-from-answer plus a recording callback are attached
Rationale: a failed call_logs insert is logged but never fails the call — telemetry must not block a live conversation
recordingStatusCallback hands the finished audio to process-call-recording
Inbound calls simul-ring every active staff browser client and, optionally, their personal phones
Super admins (tenant_id NULL) are unioned into the ring list alongside the tenant's own head_admin/admin/manager/ops users
Forwarding loop guard: a forwarding number equal to (or suffix-matching) the Twilio number is dropped so the call cannot ring itself
forwarding_caller_id_mode='business_line' shows the business number on staff phones instead of passing through the customer's
Rationale: in business_line mode the staff phone cannot resolve a contact name, so a whisper leg announces the caller before bridging
Rationale: answerOnBridge keeps the customer hearing ringback during the whisper, and is added ONLY in whisper mode to keep default behaviour unchanged
The <Dial> action URL carries tenantId/callSid/from/to/customerId/channelId into twilio-voicemail-handler when nobody answers in 30s
Preview=1 renders the exact TwiML the dev panel would get without logging a call or ringing anyone
Only a tenant with twilio_voice_enabled=true on the matched number accepts calls; anything else gets a spoken refusal
Voice status callbacks drive the call_logs state machine and stamp ended_at on terminal statuses
If no call_logs row exists for the CallSid, a minimal one is synthesised from the AccountSid with guessed direction/caller_type
A completed call is written into the conversation thread as a channel='voice' message with duration metadata
An all-zero UUID stands in for an unknown sender because chat_channel_messages.sender_id cannot be null
Whisper leg that announces the caller's name to the staff member only, then bridges the two parties
Rationale: no press-a-key screening — a Gather+Hangup makes Twilio report DialCallStatus=completed, indistinguishable from an answered call
A screened-declined call would dead-end the customer: the voicemail handler treats 'completed' as answered, so no business voicemail is offered
Safe screening requires a per-call 'screened-declined' marker shared with the voicemail handler — a schema change not yet made
CNAM caller-name display is US-only, so a spoken announcement is the only carrier-independent way to convey the name internationally
Fail OPEN: on error the whisper returns empty TwiML and connects the call rather than dropping it
test=1 renders a standalone confirmation call (announce then hang up) because there is no bridge target in a dev-panel test
Caller names are XML-escaped before entering the TwiML document
Two-phase voicemail: the Dial action plays the greeting and records, the Record action persists the recording
DialCallStatus 'completed'/'answered' is treated as answered and ends the call with no voicemail prompt
Call context (tenantId, callSid, from, to, customerId, channelId) round-trips through the TwiML action query string because Twilio holds no state
The MP3 is pulled with the TENANT's Twilio credentials and re-hosted in the 'voicemails' storage bucket so the browser needs no Twilio auth
If the re-host fails the raw Twilio URL is stored anyway — a playable-with-auth link beats losing the voicemail
The saved voicemail is back-linked to its call_logs row by twilio_call_sid after insert
The voicemail is also posted into the conversation thread as a channel='voice' message carrying the recording URL
Undo a manually recorded payment for one rental+category: unwind allocations, restore charge balances, delete or recompute the payment
The rental is read through the caller's own RLS-scoped client to prove access, then all mutations run as service_role
Refuses the undo when any Refund ledger entry exists for that category — the operator must use Refund instead
Only payments with no stripe_payment_intent_id, not Reversed and not refunding are eligible — Stripe money is never unwound locally
P&L rows are located by the composite source_ref '{paymentId}_{chargeId}' written by whoever recorded the payment
A payment left with no allocations is deleted outright; one with allocations elsewhere has remaining_amount and status recomputed to Partial/Credit/Applied
The unwind is a sequence of independent statements that 'continue' on failure — a partial undo can leave the ledger inconsistent
Replace a manager's per-tab access grants in one privileged call
A hardcoded ALLOWED_TAB_KEYS whitelist duplicating the portal's permission constants — the two must be edited together
Only an active head_admin (or a super admin) may write grants, and never across tenants
The target user's role must literally be 'manager' — granular grants exist for no other role
An empty permission array is rejected so a manager can never be saved with zero access
Grants are deleted then re-inserted without a transaction: a failed insert leaves the manager with no permissions at all
Every grant change is recorded in audit_logs with the actor, the target email and the full permission set
Card-on-file rotation for installment plans via a Stripe SetupIntent (create-setup / confirm / get-card actions)
Rationale: a stored stripe_customer_id is validated before reuse because Stripe customers are scoped per account+mode and a test-era id 500s with 'No such customer'
The SetupIntent uses usage:'off_session' because the saved card is charged unattended by the installment cron
The payment method must already belong to this Stripe customer before it is made the default
With no plan id supplied the new card is written onto every active/overdue installment plan of the customer
The tenant -> Stripe platform account / mode / Connect-options resolution block is copy-pasted four times inside this one file
Phone-side validation of the QR token handing a desktop-started AI identity verification to the customer's phone
Distinct 410 (expired) and 409 (already completed) answers so the phone page can explain exactly what went wrong
Scanning the QR flips the verification row to pending/pending, which is how the desktop page learns the phone picked it up
Returns the tenant's slug, company name and logo so the phone capture page is branded like the operator's own site
Validation neither revokes nor rotates the QR token, so the same code stays usable until it expires
Returns session_id falling back to the row id, explicitly 'for consistency with desktop' so both devices key on the same value
Unauthenticated resolution of a customer registration invite token into tenant branding and document policy
Only a 'pending' invite resolves; used or revoked links are refused with the same generic message
An expired invite is flipped to status 'expired' on read — expiry is enforced lazily, with no sweeper job
Returns the tenant's accepted_verification_document, defaulting to drivers_license, so the registration form asks for the right document
CORS headers and jsonResponse/errorResponse are re-declared inline instead of imported from _shared/cors.ts
Re-check user-edited identity fields against the document image with GPT-4o vision before accepting the edit
Names and country codes are matched loosely; dates and document numbers must match exactly
A field that cannot be read off the document returns documentValue null and matches true — benefit of the doubt on unreadable prints
approved=true only when ALL supplied fields match — a single mismatch fails the whole edit
Base64 encoding walks the buffer in 8192-byte chunks to avoid blowing the call stack on String.fromCharCode
Supabase public storage URLs are pulled through the storage API with the service role rather than a plain fetch
Model output is stripped of ``` fences before JSON.parse because the strict-JSON instruction is not always obeyed
Accepts the legacy documentImageUrl alongside documentFrontUrl so older callers keep working
Calls the OpenAI REST endpoint directly instead of the shared chatCompletion helper, but still reports cost through logExternalUsage
Veriff decision webhook: drives identity_verifications, the customer's verification status and downstream blocking
Veriff codes mapped to internal outcomes: 9001 GREEN/verified, 9102 RED/rejected, 9103 RETRY back to pending
The session id lives in payload.id for started/submitted events but in payload.verification.id for decisions
Booking-flow verifications start before a customer exists, so a decision with no matching row inserts a customer-less record to be linked later
On a terminal decision the document and face images are pulled from Veriff's media API and archived in the customer-documents bucket
Veriff media auth is an HMAC-SHA256 of the session id (list) or the media id (download), sent as X-HMAC-SIGNATURE with X-AUTH-CLIENT
The document number is checked against tenant-scoped blocked_identities and a hit overrides the decision to rejected + is_blocked
With no tenant_id on the verification the blocked-identity check is skipped entirely — a warning log, not a failure
A blocked-identity hit fans out reminder_critical notifications to every admin/head_admin of the tenant
The document number is mirrored onto customers.license_number so rental paperwork reads it without joining the verification row
An external_user_id prefixed 'additional_driver_' updates rental_additional_drivers and skips all customer-table side effects
Signature verification runs only when VERIFF_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set AND a signature header is present — unsigned posts are accepted
Unknown event shapes and missing rows are acknowledged with ok:true so Veriff never retries a payload this code cannot use
